analyst_view.overall: Early view: Game 3 at Gillette Stadium on Wednesday 2 December, only played if the series is 1-1; kick-off is still to be set and a draw goes to penalties. New England won both league meetings 2-1, but Philadelphia knocked them out in Round One in 2023. It is a short trip for Philadelphia, but both sides would be four days on from Game 2.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.0 goals. I lean lower for a decider between teams that will have met twice in 11 days: both league games were tight 2-1s, Matt Turner has been a constant in goal for New England, and neither side will want to chase the game early.

corners.text: The site expects 10.2 corners. I found nothing on either side's set pieces or wide play that moves the total, so I stay with it.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.8 cards. I lean higher for a winner-take-all third game between clubs with recent playoff history; by then both sides will carry plenty of grievances from the first two meetings.

shots.text: The site expects 26.4 shots, with 16.9 for Philadelphia away. In a decider at Gillette I expect fewer shots and a more even split, as I did for Game 1.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.6 on target. A cagey decider usually means fewer clear chances, so I lean slightly lower, even though Turner faced a lot of shots on target during the season.
